purpose: Full 11-DOF blind joint Stage-One inverse design: discover low-cement feasible basins from declared space-filling/data-anchored proposals, then confirm the lowest best-found integer level locally.
performance_optimization_fast_descriptor: src/fast_descriptors.py -- a vectorised, process-local monkey-patch replacement for stage1_evaluator.cached_descriptors (never modifies the frozen file on disk). Precomputes the fixed bin-edge-to-grid-threshold linear map once instead of a 500x6 nested Python loop per call, and computes the grid-passing curve once per candidate instead of twice (the frozen code recomputes it once per D10/D60 percentile lookup). Independently re-verified in this session against the frozen descriptors_precise on 5,000 synthetic gradations (random simplex draws, zero-mass-bin cases, exact vertices, two-bin edges): max relative difference ~1e-15, zero NaN mismatches (tests/test_fast_descriptors_equivalence.py). Installed at process start in every Phase A-D driver and in efficient_verification.py; DISABLE_FAST_DESCRIPTORS=1 opts out for a byte-for-byte comparison run if ever needed.

design_vector.representation: codec11.py stick11 codec, UNCHANGED, cement coordinate x11[0] now FREE (no fixed_cement_codec wrapper in Phases A-C).
design_vector.admissible_bounds_source: solvers_common.BND, resolved via codec11.py's shim.py import to the FROZEN research/Stage1_CA_Aware_Optimizer_20260914/run_01/src/solvers_common.py -- NOT invented or expanded for run_05.

phase_A_de_continuous_discovery.algorithm_as_originally_planned: canonical DE/rand/1/bin, repaired donor exclusion (pool excludes target index i), jittered mutation F=0.7*Uniform(0.5,1.0), binomial crossover CR=0.9 with forced jrand -- same repaired core as run_02/run_03's src/de_core.py-style loop, reused via a new src/full_de_search.py adapted from run_04/src/robust_de.py (11-D codec11 directly, cement free, no fixed_cement wrapper).
phase_A_de_continuous_discovery.algorithm_actually_used_in_the_reported_: jDE self-adaptive DE/rand/1/bin (Brest et al. 2006): identical donor selection/crossover structure, but each individual carries its own (F, CR) that self-adapts from the fitness landscape (re-randomised with small probability each generation, kept only when the resulting trial is accepted) instead of a fixed jitter schedule. Implemented as an opt-in --adaptive flag in src/full_de_search.py (default False, i.e. the originally-planned fixed-jitter scheme; ALL FOUR Phase A seeds in the reported run used --adaptive=True). This was a deliberate choice at the point of use (not a silent substitution): self-adaptive F/CR removes the need to hand-tune a fixed jitter schedule and is target-agnostic (does not encode any assumption about where the reliability boundary lies), at the cost of not being the originally pre-registered fixed-jitter DE. Documented here plainly since it is a real algorithm choice, not a bug fix or a performance-only change.
phase_A_de_continuous_discovery.objective: feasibility-first robust merit: unsupported designs are rejected; then reliability shortfall to the required target is minimized, with cement retained as a secondary gradient below the target and minimized once the target is reached. No 0.92 feasibility cliff is used.
phase_A_de_continuous_discovery.budget_note: popsize*generations+popsize = 1020 evaluations/seed (4,080 total). Benchmarked cost at N=512: 1.226s/eval SOLO. An initial attempt ran the 4 seeds as 4 parallel processes (OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 each, 8 logical cores) at popsize=25/generations=100; measured cost came back at ~8.3s/eval (gen 1 of 4 concurrent seeds: 393-438s for 50 evals each) -- roughly 6-7x the solo cost, not the expected ~1-2x, indicating the OMP/MKL thread caps were not preventing oversubscription on this machine. That run was ABORTED (traces/checkpoints removed) rather than continued at an 11-hour projected Phase-A wall time. Phase A was RELAUNCHED SEQUENTIALLY (one seed at a time, no parallelism) at the reduced popsize/generations above: 1020 evals/seed * 1.226s = ~20.8 min/seed, ~83 min total for 4 seeds. This is a documented, measured-cost-driven reduction within the driving prompt's 'roughly 3,000-5,000 evals/seed unless runtime justifies adjustment' / 'should not reproduce the earlier multi-hour optimizer zoo' guidance.

search_scenario_bank.note: ONE common-random manufacturing+residual bank shared by all 4 DE seeds and the whole Phase A stage; search-time surrogate only, never used for decisive verification.

phase_A_de_continuous_discovery.initial_population: Blind adaptive initializer (adaptive_init.py), invoked by full_de_search.py before every DE seed: 4096 scrambled-Sobol scalar samples plus simplex-aware Dirichlet(1)/Dirichlet(0.3)/data-fitted-prior gradations, 512 data-anchored perturbation/interpolation samples, fail-closed state-support screen, three common-random successive-halving rounds (64, 128, 256 scenarios), and a multi-round diverse Pareto archive with fresh global injections. No prior result coordinates are used.
phase_A_de_continuous_discovery.shortlist_retention: EVERY evaluated candidate across all generations/seeds with Rhat>=0.85 (not only the single running best) is retained in tables/DE_CONTINUOUS_SEARCH.csv, per Section 6 of the driving prompt (do not let search noise create a false minimum by discarding near-boundary candidates).

adaptive_init.scalar_design: scrambled Sobol in the six scalar unit-cube coordinates; deterministic Latin-hypercube fallback when scipy.stats.qmc is unavailable
adaptive_init.global_injection: At each refinement round, inject a fresh Sobol/Dirichlet proposal block; archive all rounds before diverse selection.
adaptive_init.timing_telemetry: Round elapsed seconds, candidate count, scenario count, and cost per candidate are written to adaptive_init_seed*_rounds.csv; every DE generation writes the same fields plus accepted count and cumulative evaluations.

search_safety_margin.note: The search target equals the required reliability. Statistical conservatism belongs to final decisive verification; a harder search threshold can erase valid low-cement basins before refinement.

phase_B_rescreen.purpose: Deduplicate near-identical DE solutions and rescore leading candidates on a FRESH, LARGER, common-random bank disjoint from the Phase A search bank, before committing to NOMAD starts.
phase_B_rescreen.dedup_rule: two candidates are locally near-identical if their codec11 encode11() L2 distance < 0.1 (11-D unit-cube coordinates), using the original greedy local-basin representatives. For every local basin retain BOTH its lower-cement boundary representative and its maximum Phase-A-Rhat representative (one record if identical). This post-Phase-A correction avoids discarding a higher-cement feasible seed merely because cement is the minimisation variable. On the 918-row shortlist it retains 31 candidates: 16 boundary representatives plus 15 distinct reliability seeds.

rescreen_bank.note: disjoint from the Phase A search seed (205609151) and from every decisive-verification seed.

phase_B_rescreen.candidates_rescreened: every DE shortlist entry (Rhat_search>=threshold at N=512) after deduplication; weaker near-misses remain diagnostic/continuation records but cannot be final selections.
phase_B_rescreen.selection_for_phase_C: top 6-10 distinct basins by (support/domain validity, then Phase-B Rhat feasibility, then minimum cement) -- never by gradation shape.

phase_C_nomad_refinement.algorithm: genuine PyNomad MADS, full 11-D (codec11 directly, cement free -- NOT fixed_cement_codec).
phase_C_nomad_refinement.starts: every distinct supported feasible DE_dedup basin selected in Phase B (target 6-10); infeasible points are continuation diagnostics only. F1: feasible-only best (x_single_best infeasible never promoted). W1 gradation gate as 4th PB constraint (TASK A2).

search_scenario_bank.note: fresh common-random bank for Phase C, disjoint from Phase A (205609151), Phase B (205609201), and every decisive-verification seed.

phase_C_nomad_refinement.output: best-found CONTINUOUS frontier candidate(s) -- reported as a best-found frontier region, never as an exact decimal-precision optimum (Section 14 of the driving prompt).

phase_D_integer_cement_profile.purpose: 1 kg/m3-resolution fixed-cement verification profile around the continuous frontier located in Phases A-C, to answer 'why not 266 or 271' with an adjacent-integer FAIL/PASS bracket rather than a fabricated decimal.
phase_D_integer_cement_profile.codec: src/fixed_cement_codec.py (reused unchanged from run_04) wrapping codec11.py -- cement pinned exactly per tested integer level, all other 10 variables free and RE-OPTIMIZED at every level (never copied unchanged from the continuous result).
phase_D_integer_cement_profile.window_selection: Only entered after Phase C finds a state-supported continuous candidate at or above the required search reliability. Start at its floor integer, test lower levels in a 10 kg/m3 coarse descent, then re-optimise only the final 1 kg/m3 bracket. A plainly implausible search result may skip decisive verification; it can never pass a candidate. Global fixed-cement discovery (blind_repair.fixed_cement_discovery) now runs first when continuous discovery is empty, so Phase D is no longer gated on a single continuous basin.
phase_D_integer_cement_profile.starts_per_level: strongest distinct supported feasible Phase-C basins from this run; infeasible points are never promoted. F1 feasible-only; Phase D re-optimises all 10 free vars per level.

search_scenario_bank.note: disjoint from every other search/verification seed in this contract.

phase_D_integer_cement_profile.stopping_rule: Stop with an explicit negative decision if blind discovery finds no feasible basin. Otherwise identify the lowest locally profiled integer whose independently re-optimized candidate decisively passes and confirm the immediately lower integer outcome after its own re-optimization. No upward scan from a failed basin is allowed.

excluded_variables: no variable outside the 11-DOF Stage-One design vector is introduced; no gradation-shape penalty, smoothness preference, zero-bin penalty, sand preference, or aesthetic tie-breaker of any kind (tests/test_no_gradation_penalty.py, reused unchanged, still enforced).
